requirements.evidence: .env.example:1,7-8 sets APP_NAME=PegaFila, APP_LOCALE=pt_BR and keeps APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE=en; phpunit.xml:21-23 pins the same three values. config/mail.php:128-133 sets mail.markdown.theme=pegafila and resources/views/vendor/mail/html/themes/pegafila.css:240-242 paints .button-primary/.button-blue with #0f7490 (the action button exists in both mails). lang/pt_BR.json:559,804 add 'Reset your password' and 'Verify your email address'. routes/web.php:16-31 defines all five named routes with the required middleware (guest, throttle:6,1, auth+signed+throttle). NewPasswordController.php:30-51 validates via ResetPasswordRequest, resets through the broker, rotates remember_token, fires PasswordReset and redirects to '/' with the status; PasswordResetLinkController.php:24-33 validates, sends only for real users and always flashes passwords.sent; VerifyEmailController.php:15-19 fulfils the request and redirects to '/'. Both required views exist and the reset form has a single email input (reset-password.blade.php:23-64).

conventions.evidence: HTTP validation follows the documented split: inline $request->validate for one field (PasswordResetLinkController.php:26-28) and a generated-style Form Request for the 3-field reset (app/Http/Requests/ResetPasswordRequest.php:26-34). Docs are kept in sync (CHANGELOG.md:12-14,21; docs/business-rules.md:68-73). Views use semantic Bulma markup with labels, autocomplete and aria roles, escape with {{ }} and include @csrf (forgot-password.blade.php:30-44, reset-password.blade.php:23-64), and each rendered view has a feature test asserting status and key markup. One deviation: both auth views copy the same full-page shell (head/meta, Vite-or-CDN fallback, section/container/box) instead of extracting a shared anonymous Blade component as the conventions prefer (forgot-password.blade.php:1-20 and reset-password.blade.php:1-20).

security.evidence: All four reset routes are guests-only (routes/web.php:16) and the request endpoint is throttled to 6/min (routes/web.php:20) as is the verification link (routes/web.php:30). Reset input is fully server-side validated, including Password::min(8)->letters()->mixedCase()->numbers()->confirmed (ResetPasswordRequest.php:26-34); known and unknown addresses get the identical status flash, so the form cannot enumerate accounts (PasswordResetLinkController.php:30-32). The verification URL is signed and EmailVerificationRequest::authorize rejects a mismatched id/hash with 403 before fulfill() (VerifyEmailController.php:15-19; tests cover wrong hash, other user id, unsigned and expired links). Forms carry @csrf and all dynamic output is escaped with {{ }} (forgot-password.blade.php:30-44, reset-password.blade.php:23-64); password and remember_token are written through forceFill only (NewPasswordController.php:34-37). No weakness found.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/PasswordResetTest.php:14-201 covers the form, registered vs unknown address, email validation, the 6/min throttle, token/email mismatch, cross-account token attempts, every password rule, remember-token rotation, the PasswordReset event and authenticated users being redirected away. tests/Feature/EmailVerificationTest.php:10-83 covers success, wrong hash, another user's id, unsigned and expired links, and already-verified users. tests/Feature/AccountEmailsTest.php:7-51 asserts the locale/name pins, the pegafila theme config and both pt-BR mails (subject, action text, greeting, translated body, absence of the English sub-copy and the brand colour surviving inlining). Tests are meaningful and none are weakened or removed.

simplicity.evidence: The change reuses Laravel's Password broker, EmailVerificationRequest and markdown mailer instead of reimplementing them (PasswordResetLinkController.php:30, NewPasswordController.php:31-42, VerifyEmailController.php:17), and the controllers stay at 21-52 lines. The mail theme is a custom-theme copy, which is inherent to the feature. The one avoidable duplication is the page shell repeated between resources/views/auth/forgot-password.blade.php:1-20 and resources/views/auth/reset-password.blade.php:1-20.

readability.evidence: Small, focused methods with one-line docblocks explain intent (NewPasswordController.php:27-51, PasswordResetLinkController.php:20-33); names are intention-revealing (PasswordResetLinkController, NewPasswordController, ResetPasswordRequest) and the test helper verificationUrl(EmailVerificationTest.php:10-19) removes repeated URL-building noise. The new lang keys are inserted in the file's existing alphabetical order (lang/pt_BR.json:559,804) and there is no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: The diff is limited to the requested deliverable: env/phpunit locale pins, the pegafila theme and mail config, the two auth views, the pt-BR keys, routes/controllers/Form Request, feature tests, and the CHANGELOG/business-rules updates the conventions require. The only model change is implementing MustVerifyEmail (app/Models/User.php:5,15), which VerifyEmail needs. No login, registration, /home, Livewire, SCSS/JS or Docker work was added.

issues.explanation: Both auth pages repeat the same full-page shell (head/meta, Vite-or-CDN Bulma fallback, section/container/box), which the conventions would rather see extracted into a small anonymous Blade component.

The brand-colour assertions depend on the inlined style attribute coming after class and on the exact '#0f7490' spelling, so they could break on a harmless change to Laravel's button markup or the theme while the behaviour is still correct.

review.summary: The change implements the whole pt-BR account-email task: locale/name pins, a pegafila markdown theme using #0f7490 on the action button, translated reset and verification notifications, the guests-only throttled password-reset flow, and the signed verification link, all backed by thorough feature tests. Requirements, security and test coverage are strong, and only a small duplication of the auth page shell (plus a slightly brittle inline-style assertion) keeps it from being an unconditional approve.
